context: Each item can be taken at most once. The diagram uses the same separate example as the preceding tree: three items with weights 10, 20, 20 and values 60, 110, 120, and cap = 30 (see table). dp[i, c] denotes the maximum value for the first i items at available capacity c. The columns are labeled wgt[i] and val[i] (i from 1 to 3), while the code uses array index i-1.

When the current item fits, take the larger of dp[i-1, c] for skipping it and dp[i-1, c-wgt[i-1]] + val[i-1] for taking it. If it does not fit, only the skip branch is available. With no items (i = 0) or no capacity (c = 0), return 0.
description: From root dp[3, 30], consider items 3, 2, and 1 in order. Item 2 (watermelon) and item 3 (pineapple) both weigh 20. Skipping 3 then taking 2 and taking 3 then skipping 2 both leave capacity 10 with only item 1 (apple, weight 10, value 60) available. The paths meet at dp[1, 10].

The left subtree first visits dp[1, 10] along “skip 3→take 2.” It compares dp[0, 10] with dp[0, 0] + 60 and caches the result. In the right subtree, skipping item 2 at dp[2, 10] reaches dp[1, 10] again (“take 3→skip 2”). The label “Prune: cached result found” means the search returns the cached value without expanding the two leaves again. Item 1 has weight 10 and value 60, so the cached result is 60. This number follows from the input table and is not a node label.

At dp[2, 10] in the right subtree, both branches have scissors but stop for different reasons. The left branch dp[1, 10] hits the cache and returns 60, a valid solution. The right branch dp[1, -10] (“Prune: item weight > knapsack capacity”) is an illustrative invalid node: item 2 weighs 20, exceeding the remaining capacity of 10. The program checks the weight before recursing and calls only the skip branch dp[1, 10]. It never calls dp[1, -10].
The tables below list the input for this example and the full recursion tree as drawn. Row headers give the choices from the root to distinguish separate occurrences of a state.

frames.explanation: The figure has 11 nodes, with 4 base-case leaves instead of 6 in the brute-force tree. Taking items 1 and 3 still gives the overall maximum of 180. Both the cached 60 and the optimum 180 follow from the input data and are not labeled on the nodes.
frames.title: Reusing dp[1, 10] on a cache hit and distinguishing it from overweight pruning

summary: When the path taking item 3 encounters dp[1, 10] again, it returns the cached value without repeating the subtree. This differs from pruning an overweight item.
